Award/Judgment Factual Position & Pleadings
1.

This Dar was filed on 01/04/2022 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties of
this case.
The Dar is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 25.10
.2021 in which one Master Bantu S/o Sh. Mukesh (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") lost his life.

As per DAR, at about 17.45 hours, on 25.10.2021, the deceased was walking near Parshvnath Building, Chappin Phari Road, Aruna Nagar, Majnu Ka Tilla, Delhi (falling within the jurisdiction of PS Civil Lines) in the meantime, he got crushed by a TATA 407 bearing registration No. DL-1AD-6530 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle"), which was being driven at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner by its driver.

The injured was immediately removed to Aruna Asaf Ali Hospital for medical treatment where he was declared dead, postmortem was conducted and the offending vehicle was seized by the police from the spot of accident.
An FIR No. 426/21, PS Timarpur, U/s 279/304A IPC was registered by police regarding MACT No. 345/22 Sunita & Ors.

7. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
" Whether the deceased Bantu suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 25.10.2021 at about 17.45 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No.

8. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil MACT No. 345/22 Sunita & Ors. Vs. Shree Ram & Ors.

Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the deceased at the relevant time.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

13. In view of the PM report of deceased placed on record by the petitioners as Ex. PW1/4(colly), no dispute is left regarding the death of the deceased on account of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.
14. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on account of neglect and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioners.

PECUNIARY DAMAGES, NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES (INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS)
16.
Hon'ble Delhi High Court has prescribed the method of computation of compensation in cases where minor children have lost their lives in motor vehicle accident in Chetan Malhotra and Ors.

Vs.
Lala Ram and Ors., MANU/DE/1545/2016 decided on 13.05.2016 The Hon'ble Delhi High Court has passed the following directions in para no. 69 of Chetan Malhotra (supra).

The same is reproduced below for ready reference :-
69.

Subject to all other requisite conditions being fulfilled, for the foregoing reasons,
in order to bring about consistency and uniformity in approach to the issue, it is held that claims for compensation on account of death of children shall be determined as follows:
(i) Till such time as the law is amended by the Legislature, or the Central Government notifies the amendment to the Second Schedule in exercise of the enabling power vested in it by Section 163A(3) of the MACT No. 345/22 Sunita & Ors. Vs. Shree Ram & Ors.

(v) For assessment of the pecuniary damages on account of the death of children up to the age of 10 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated, capitalizing the multiplicand, by applying the multiplier of ten (10).

(vi) For children of the age-group of more than 10 years up to 15 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated by applying the multiplier of fifteen (15).
(vii) For children of the age-group of more than 15 years but less than 18 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated by applying the multiplier of eighteen (18).

18. PW-1 Smt. Sunita has placed on record the copy of Aadhar Card of deceased Ex. PW1/2, as per which, the date of birth of deceased was 12.09.2012.
Apparently, the deceased was aged 09 years at the time of his death (i.e. on 25.10.2021).
Since the deceased was aged less than 10 years at the time of his death, multiplier of '10' is applicable.
19. CBDT has notified the CII vide circular bearing no. SO1790(E) on 05.06.2017.
The major change in this notification is the introduction of new base year as financial year 2001-2002 instead of financial year 1981-1982.
CII has been notified as 317 for the financial year 2021-22 and the CII for the base year 2001-2002 is 100.

Accordingly, the inflation corrected notional income of deceased works out as Rs.48,000/- (rounded off of Rs.47,550) (Rupees Forty Eight Thousand only) (Rs.
15,000/- X 317 / 100) per annum.
As observed earlier, multiplier of 10 is applicable and 1/3rd of the notional income is to be deducted towards personal living expenses.
Accordingly, the pecuniary loss to the estate turns out to be Rs. 3,20,000/- (Rs. 48,000/- X 2/3 X 10).
Upon an equivalent amount being added towards composite non- pecuniary damages, the total compensation payable comes to be Rs.6,40,000/- (Rs. 3,20,000/- X 2).
The said amount is admissible to the petitioners as a compensation.
Further, in terms of propositions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
" Whether the deceased Bantu suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 25.10.2021 at about 17.45 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-1LA-D-6530 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent No.2 and insured with the Respondent No. 3? OPP.''
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
Subject to all other requisite conditions being fulfilled, for the foregoing reasons,
in order to bring about consistency and uniformity in approach to the issue, it is held that claims for compensation on account of death of children shall be determined as follows:
(i) Till such time as the law is amended by the Legislature, or the Central Government notifies the amendment to the Second Schedule in exercise of the enabling power vested in it by Section 163A(3) of the MACT No. 345/22 Sunita & Ors. Vs. Shree Ram & Ors.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil MACT No. 345/22 Sunita & Ors. Vs. Shree Ram & Ors.
and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
11.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was involved in a collision with the deceased at the relevant time.
12. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending MACT No. 345/22 Sunita & Ors. Vs. Shree Ram & Ors.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the deceased at the relevant time.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
As this Tribunal has already held that R1 was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his rashness and negligence in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time, therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Since the deceased was aged less than 10 years at the time of his death, multiplier of '10' is applicable.
The maturity amounts of the FDR(s) be credit by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the petitioner(s) near the place of their residence.
However, since the offending vehicle was insured with R-3 at the time of accident, therefore, R-3/ Insurance Company is liable to indemnify R-2 in respect of above liability.
